Agent.description:
Serializes Agent model instances to JSON and validates data for creating
or updating Agent instances.

This serializer provides a comprehensive representation of an Agent,
including its type, endpoint, and nested details for related 'organization'
and 'owner' for read operations, while allowing 'organization' and 'owner' IDs
for write operations.

Attributes:
    organization_detail (OrganizationMinimalSerializer): Read-only nested
        serializer for the agent's organization. Displays minimal details.
    owner_detail (UserProfileMinimalSerializer): Read-only nested serializer
        for the agent's owner's user profile. Displays minimal details.
        Can be null if the agent has no owner or the owner has no profile.
    agent_type (CharField): The type of the agent as a string
                      (e.g., LITELLM, OPENAI_SDK, GOOGLE_ADK).

Meta:
    model (Agent): The model class that this serializer works with.
    fields (tuple): The fields to include in the serialized output.
        Includes standard Agent fields like 'endpoint', 'type',
        and the read-only nested details.
    read_only_fields (tuple): Fields that are read-only and cannot be
        set during create/update operations through this serializer.
        This includes 'id', 'created_at', 'updated_at', and the
        nested detail fields.

name.description: Display name, unique within the organization.
name.title: Agent Name

endpoint.description: Copy of `config.connection.endpoint`; empty when it has none.
endpoint.title: Endpoint URL

config.description: The agent's model configuration, as the hackagent SDK reads it: `name` (the model), `connection` (`provider`, `type`, and optionally `endpoint`, `api_key`, `headers`, `timeout`) and optionally `generation` and `options`. `connection.api_key` must be a `${VARIABLE}` reference to an organization secret; literal credentials are refused.

organization_detail.description: The organization the agent belongs to.

owner.description: Id of the user who created the agent.

owner_detail.description: The user who created the agent; null if unknown.

updated_at.description: When the agent was last changed.

info.description:
The HackAgent API stores the agents you red-team, the campaigns you run
against them and everything those runs record (results, traces, reports). It
also serves the HackAgent LLM gateway, the attacker and judge models that
campaigns use. The `hackagent` SDK and CLI and the HackAgent dashboard are
built on it.

## Base URL

The hosted service is at `https://api.hackagent.dev`; paths in this reference
are relative to it (for example `https://api.hackagent.dev/agent`). A
self-hosted installation serves the same paths under its own address, usually
behind `/api`.

## Authentication

Every endpoint needs a bearer token in the `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer <your HackAgent API key>
```

- **API keys** are created in the dashboard (or with `POST /key`) and shown
  once. They act as the user who created them, within that user's
  organization. Use them for the SDK, the CLI and scripts.
- **Login tokens** (Auth0 on the hosted service, Keycloak on self-hosted
  installations) are what the dashboard sends. A few account endpoints accept
  only login tokens: API keys cannot create other keys, read usage logs or
  manage the account, and get `401` there.
- **Run tokens** (`hart_<prefix>.<secret>`) are issued to a cloud run when it
  is claimed and expire when it finishes. They can only report on that run
  and call the LLM gateway.
- The **worker token** is the cloud worker's service credential; it can only
  claim cloud runs.

A missing, malformed, expired or revoked credential gets `401`.

## Organizations

Everything belongs to an organization. Each user belongs to one, and the API
only shows and changes objects of the caller's organization: objects of other
organizations answer `404`. Staff accounts of an installation also see the
agents, attacks, runs and results of every organization.

## Pagination

List endpoints return a page:
`{"count": 42, "next": "<url>", "previous": null, "results": [...]}`. Ask for
another page with `page` (1-based). Endpoints that accept `page_size` say so,
with their maximum; the default page size is 10. `next` and `previous` are
ready-to-use URLs, or `null` at either end.

## Errors

Errors are JSON. Validation failures (`400`) map each invalid field to a list
of messages, for example `{"name": ["This field is required."]}`; errors that
are not about one field use `non_field_errors`, and nested configuration
errors are keyed by their dotted path (`"connection.api_key"`). Other errors
carry a human-readable `detail`, and often a machine-readable `code`:

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `400` | The request is invalid; nothing was changed. |
| `401` | Missing or invalid credential, or a credential type the endpoint refuses. |
| `402` | Not enough credits for an LLM gateway call. |
| `403` | The credential may not do this, or the installation is read-only because its license is not valid (`code: license_read_only`). |
| `404` | No such object in the caller's organization. |
| `409` | The run is not in a state that allows the call (already claimed, finished, still active). |
| `429` | Rate limited; retry after the seconds in the `Retry-After` header. |

The LLM gateway (`/v1/...`) answers errors in its own shape,
`{"error": "...", "code": "..."}`, as OpenAI-compatible clients expect.

## Credits

Each organization has a balance of credits, in US dollars (see
`GET /organization/me`). Calls to the LLM gateway, made by you or by a cloud
run on your behalf, are charged to it: before a call, its maximum cost is
checked against the balance (`402` if the balance cannot cover it), and its
actual cost is deducted afterwards. A cloud launch needs a
minimum balance. Ask for more with `POST /credits/request`.

## Rate limits

Requests are rate limited per user (by default 1,000 an hour); cloud runs have
their own, larger budget per run token, and the campaign run report reads
another one per user. A limited request gets
`429` with a `Retry-After` header.

post.description:
The HackAgent LLM gateway, in OpenAI's chat completions format: point an OpenAI client at `https://api.hackagent.dev/v1` with a HackAgent API key. `model` picks one of HackAgent's models (`GET /v1/models`): `hackagent/attacker-v1`, which writes adversarial prompts, or `hackagent/judge-v1`, which judges responses. The response names that model only, never the upstream one.

Each call is charged to the organization's credits: its maximum cost (from `max_tokens`, capped at the model's limit) must be covered by the balance (402 otherwise), and its actual cost is deducted after it succeeds and logged (`GET /apilogs`). Streaming is not available (`stream: true` answers 501). Accepts an API key, a login token, or a cloud run's token, whose calls are charged to the run's organization. Errors use the gateway's own shape, `{"error": ..., "code": ...}`.

400.description: Invalid body: not JSON, an unknown `model` (`UNKNOWN_MODEL`) or an invalid `max_tokens` (`INVALID_MAX_TOKENS`).

401.description: Missing, invalid, expired or revoked credential, or a credential this endpoint does not accept.

value.details: Estimated cost: 0.012000 USD, Available: 0.004000 USD. Please add credits to continue.

402.description: Not enough credits for the call (`INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS`).

403.description: The caller has no organization to charge (`ORG_CONTEXT_MISSING`), or the credential may not call the gateway.

429.description: The model provider is busy (`PROVIDER_RATE_LIMITED`), or the caller is rate limited; retry after `Retry-After` seconds.

500.description: The gateway is misconfigured or failed unexpectedly.

502.description: The model provider could not be reached or failed.
